sop_modules.name: Mobilization, Access & Equipment Staging
sop_modules.description: Crew mobilization, equipment staging, access setup. No warranty void gate (aluminum siding warranties have typically expired). No LRV verification gate (aluminum has no LRV restriction — any color permitted).

tasks.name: Crew Mobilization & Equipment Staging
tasks.description: Mobilize crew, transport materials and equipment to site. Stage self-etching primer, epoxy intermediate (if coastal), finish paint, spray equipment, DFT gauge, abrasive pads, and protection materials at work area. Verify material against spec — confirm self-etching primer (phosphoric acid + zinc), NOT STIX adhesion primer or bonding primer. Confirm acrylic latex finish.

quality_notes.all: All materials on-site and verified against scope. Self-etching primer confirmed — NOT STIX or bonding primer. DFT gauge present. Equipment in working order.

tasks.name: Scaffold / Lift Setup
tasks.description: Erect scaffold, position aerial lift, or stage extension ladders per access plan. OSHA-compliant setup with fall protection. Scaffold preferred over ladder for multi-story aluminum to improve spray stability for DFT control.

quality_notes.all: Level, plumb, tied off. Fall protection in place. Base plates on firm footing. Scaffold preferred for multi-story to improve DFT control stability.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Mobilize → Scaffold/lift setup. No warranty void gate (aluminum siding). No LRV verification gate (no LRV restriction on aluminum).

sop_modules.name: Exterior Protection Setup
sop_modules.description: Deploy landscape, hardscape, window/door masking, trim masking, fixture covers, and HVAC protection. Spray method requires full masking of windows, doors, and trim. No RRP containment needed (aluminum factory-baked enamel is not lead-based). Extended landscape protection for chalk-laden wash runoff.

tasks.name: Landscape Protection
tasks.description: Deploy plastic sheeting and drop cloths over landscape beds, shrubs, and plantings adjacent to working elevations. Protects from pressure wash runoff (chalk-laden alkaline cleaner), primer drips, and spray overspray. Extended coverage for aluminum — wash runoff contains more chalk residue than vinyl.

quality_notes.all: Secure tarps at grade. Extend 3 ft minimum from foundation for brush/roll, 10 ft for spray overspray zone. Extra runoff protection for wash phase — chalk-laden alkaline cleaner stains plantings.

tasks.name: Hardscape Protection
tasks.description: Deploy drop cloths and plastic sheeting on walkways, patios, and driveways adjacent to working elevations. Chalk-laden wash runoff stains concrete — drop cloths at foundation line critical.

quality_notes.all: Tape plastic to foundation at grade line. Extend to drip/overspray zone. Pre-wet hardscape before wash phase to reduce chalk staining risk.

tasks.name: Window Masking (Spray)
tasks.description: Mask all windows on working elevations with masking paper/film and tape. Required for spray application method to prevent overspray on glass and frames.

quality_notes.all: Full glass and frame coverage. Tape sealed at edges — no overspray paths. Paper/film extends past frame to siding overlap.

tasks.name: Door Masking (Spray)
tasks.description: Mask all exterior doors on working elevations with plastic sheeting and tape. Required for spray application.

quality_notes.all: Full door coverage including hardware. Maintain access for occupants where possible.

tasks.name: Trim Masking at Siding-to-Trim Transition
tasks.description: Tape and mask corner trim, window casing, and door casing where trim is a different color from siding. Prevents siding paint on trim surfaces during spray.

quality_notes.all: Tape line clean and straight. Paper extends 3-6 inches from edge. No exposed trim surface in spray zone.

tasks.name: Light Fixture Masking
tasks.description: Bag and tape exterior light fixtures on working elevations.

quality_notes.all: Complete coverage. Secure tape to prevent seepage during wash and spray.

tasks.name: HVAC Unit Cover
tasks.description: Cover HVAC condenser units adjacent to working elevations with plastic sheeting.

quality_notes.all: Full cover during active work. Remove promptly after — do not leave covered overnight in warm weather.

tasks.name: Utility Panel Masking
tasks.description: Mask electrical panels, gas meters, and utility boxes on working elevations.

quality_notes.all: Complete coverage. Do not obstruct access to emergency shutoffs.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Landscape → Hardscape → Window mask (spray) → Door mask (spray) → Trim mask (spray) → Light fixtures → HVAC → Utility panels. Protection BEFORE any wash or coating work. Extended landscape coverage for chalk-laden wash runoff.

sop_modules.name: Pressure Wash with TSP / Alkaline Cleaner
sop_modules.description: Mandatory pressure wash to remove dirt, mildew, and chalk residue from aluminum surface. First production step. chalk_severity drives wash intensity: none = standard wash; light = TSP + chalk removal focus; heavy = multiple passes + mechanical scrubbing + extended dwell time. Must dry 24-48 hours before scuffing/priming.

tasks.name: Mix Alkaline Cleaning Solution
tasks.description: Mix TSP or dedicated aluminum siding cleaner concentrate with water per manufacturer directions. Load into pressure washer downstream injector or pump sprayer for pre-treatment. Increase concentration for heavy chalk projects per manufacturer guidance.

quality_notes.all: Mix ratio per manufacturer. Higher concentration for heavy chalk. Solution ready before starting wash.

tasks.name: Pressure Wash Aluminum Siding — Standard
tasks.description: Pressure wash all siding surfaces using downward spray pattern. 1000-1500 PSI — aluminum is more durable than vinyl but do not exceed 2000 PSI to avoid denting thin-gauge panels. Remove dirt, mildew, and surface contamination. Work top-down, one elevation at a time.

block_when.note: High wind disperses wash water and cleaner onto adjacent properties

quality_notes.QT2: 1000-1200 PSI. Remove visible dirt and mildew. Allow 24 hr dry minimum.
quality_notes.QT3: 1000-1500 PSI with TSP solution. Thorough surface cleaning. Allow 24-48 hr dry.

tasks.name: Pressure Wash — Light Chalk Removal
tasks.description: Pressure wash with TSP/alkaline cleaner at increased concentration for light chalk removal. Apply cleaner via downstream injector, allow 5-10 minute dwell time, then rinse at 1000-1500 PSI downward pattern. Focus on south/west facades where chalk is heaviest.

quality_notes.all: TSP solution at standard concentration. 5-10 min dwell time. Rinse at 1000-1500 PSI. Focus south/west facades.

tasks.name: Pressure Wash — Heavy Chalk Removal (Multi-Pass)
tasks.description: Extended wash protocol for heavy chalk. Multiple passes with TSP/alkaline cleaner at increased concentration. First pass: apply cleaner, 10-15 minute dwell, pressure rinse. Second pass: mechanical scrubbing with soft-bristle brush on stubborn areas. Third pass: final rinse. Extended dwell time between passes. Significantly more labor than standard wash.

quality_notes.all: Multiple wash passes required. Mechanical scrubbing on stubborn chalk. Extended dwell time. Complete chalk removal mandatory — re-wash areas that fail verification.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Mix cleaner → Select wash task by chalk_severity (standard OR light chalk OR heavy chalk multi-pass) → Dry 24-48 hr. Do NOT proceed to prep or prime until surface is completely dry. chalk_severity modifier (FAC_ALRP_CHALK) scales wash labor: none=1.00, light=1.25, heavy=1.75.

sop_modules.name: Surface Preparation — Chalk Verify, Oxide Scuff, Spot Caulk
sop_modules.description: Mandatory chalk verification gate (all projects, all substrate states), oxide layer scuff with synthetic abrasive pads (180-320 grit) to break Al2O3 film, post-scuff dust cleanup, and spot caulk (QT3 only). CRITICAL TIMING: prime within 4-8 hours of scuff (2-4 hours coastal) — aluminum re-oxidizes rapidly.

tasks.name: Chalk Verification Gate
tasks.description: After siding has dried from wash, perform hand-rub chalk verification test on all elevations. Rub dark cloth firmly across surface — any white powder transfer indicates incomplete chalk removal. This is a MANDATORY GATE for ALL projects, ALL substrate states including SS_EXT_SOUND_PAINT. Residual chalk is a bond-breaker for self-etching primer. Re-wash any areas that fail.

substrate_state_rules.note: MANDATORY for ALL substrate states. Even sound-paint state may have hidden chalk in sheltered areas.

quality_notes.QT2: Test 2+ areas per elevation. Re-wash if chalk transfer detected.
quality_notes.QT3: Test 3+ areas per elevation including sheltered recesses. Document results. Re-wash if any chalk transfer detected.

tasks.name: Oxide Layer Scuff — Break Al2O3 Film
tasks.description: Scuff all siding surfaces with synthetic steel wool or 180-320 grit abrasive pads to mechanically break the aluminum oxide (Al2O3) layer. This is MORE aggressive than vinyl scuff — purpose is to fracture the oxide film so self-etching primer acid can reach base aluminum. Use ONLY synthetic pads — real steel wool leaves ferrous particles that cause galvanic corrosion (rust spots). TIMING CRITICAL: self-etching primer must be applied within 4-8 hours of scuffing (2-4 hours in coastal/humid environments) because aluminum re-oxidizes rapidly.

substrate_state_rules.note: SS_EXT_CHALKING state requires more aggressive scuffing after chalk removal — surface is more weathered. Modifier stacks with FAC_ALRP_CHALK on this task.

quality_notes.QT2: Scuff visible oxide and high-gloss areas. Focus on elevation faces with most weathering.
quality_notes.QT3: Full-surface scuff on all elevations. Uniform matte appearance after scuffing. No glossy areas remaining.

tasks.name: Post-Scuff Dust Cleanup
tasks.description: Remove all scuffing dust, aluminum oxide particles, and residue from siding surfaces before priming. Compressed air or tack wipe. Critical — aluminum dust on surface reduces primer bond.

quality_notes.all: No visible dust or residue. Surface ready for self-etching primer. Compressed air preferred for speed on large areas.

tasks.name: Caulk Assessment at Siding-to-Trim Joints
tasks.description: Inspect existing caulk at siding-to-trim joints, J-channels, and penetrations. Mark failed or missing caulk for replacement. QT3 only. Aluminum has minimal thermal movement at joints — polyurethane not required.

quality_notes.QT3: Inspect all siding-to-trim joints. Mark failed caulk with tape flag. Document scope.

tasks.name: Spot Caulk Replacement
tasks.description: Remove failed caulk and apply new siliconized acrylic paintable caulk at siding-to-trim joints. QT3 only. Allow cure per manufacturer spec before top-coating. Siliconized acrylic is sufficient — aluminum has minimal thermal movement.

quality_notes.QT3: Clean joint, apply consistent bead, tool smooth. No voids. Allow cure time before primer.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Chalk verify gate (MANDATORY, all projects) → Oxide scuff → Dust cleanup → Caulk assess (QT3) → Caulk apply (QT3). CRITICAL: proceed to prime module SAME DAY as scuff — aluminum re-oxidizes within 4-8 hours (2-4 hours coastal). Caulk must cure before primer coat.

sop_modules.name: Self-Etching Primer Application
sop_modules.description: Self-etching primer (phosphoric acid + zinc) spray application. Single coat. DFT 0.5-1.0 mil MAXIMUM — over-application causes cohesive failure within the primer film. Fine-atomization spray tips required. Single-pass technique. ALWAYS required regardless of substrate state. FUNDAMENTALLY different from STIX adhesion primer (vinyl). Must be applied same day as oxide scuff.

tasks.name: Self-Etching Primer — Spray Application
tasks.description: Spray-apply self-etching primer (phosphoric acid + zinc chromate) to all aluminum siding surfaces. Full coverage, single coat. DFT 0.5-1.0 mil ONLY — over-application above 1.0 mil causes COHESIVE FAILURE within the primer film. Use fine-atomization spray tips (311-413). Single-pass technique — do NOT double-back. No backbrushing — aluminum is non-porous metal.

quality_notes.all: DFT 0.5-1.0 mil ONLY. Fine-atomization tips. Single-pass — no double-back. No runs, sags, or holidays. Verify DFT with wet film gauge during application. Lead skill level — DFT control is critical.

tasks.name: Self-Etching Primer — Brush/Roll Application
tasks.description: Brush and roll self-etching primer when spray is not feasible (high wind, neighbor proximity). Roller with 3/8 inch nap for open field, brush at edges and J-channels. Thin application — DFT 0.5-1.0 mil ONLY. More difficult to control DFT with roller than spray.

quality_notes.all: DFT 0.5-1.0 mil ONLY. Thin coats — roller tends to over-apply. Verify DFT frequently. Even application. No holidays.

tasks.name: DFT Verification — Self-Etching Primer
tasks.description: Verify dry film thickness of self-etching primer using magnetic/eddy-current DFT gauge after primer has cured. Target: 0.5-1.0 mil. Over-application (>1.0 mil) causes cohesive failure — re-work required if DFT exceeds maximum. Test minimum 3 locations per elevation. Document DFT readings.

quality_notes.QT2: Test 2+ locations per elevation. Document max DFT reading. Flag areas >1.0 mil.
quality_notes.QT3: Test 3+ locations per elevation. Document all readings. Any area >1.0 mil requires investigation. Under 0.5 mil requires touch-up.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Self-etching primer is ALWAYS required — no skip option. Method determined by application_method dimension. DFT verification after cure. Allow cure per TDS before epoxy intermediate (coastal) or finish coat. SAME DAY as oxide scuff — do NOT delay.

sop_modules.name: Epoxy Intermediate Coat (Coastal Only)
sop_modules.description: Two-component epoxy primer intermediate coat applied between self-etching primer and acrylic topcoat. CONDITIONAL — only when site environment is coastal/marine (salt-air exposure). Creates three-layer corrosion barrier system. Applied over cured self-etching primer.

tasks.name: Epoxy Intermediate — Spray Application
tasks.description: Spray-apply two-component epoxy primer over cured self-etching primer. Single coat per manufacturer spec. Creates chemical-resistant barrier against salt penetration. Verify inter-coat compatibility with self-etching primer below and acrylic topcoat above.

quality_notes.all: Apply over cured self-etching primer. Even mil build per manufacturer PDS. Verify pot life for two-component mix. Lead skill level — specialty product.

tasks.name: Epoxy Intermediate — Brush/Roll Application
tasks.description: Brush and roll epoxy intermediate when spray is not feasible. Roller for open field, brush at edges.

quality_notes.all: Apply over cured self-etching primer. Even application. Monitor pot life.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: COASTAL ONLY — skip entirely for non-coastal projects. Applied after self-etching primer has cured. Allow cure per TDS before acrylic topcoat.

sop_modules.name: Finish Coat 1
sop_modules.description: First finish coat application. 100% acrylic latex exterior. Spray is primary method. No backbrushing — aluminum is non-porous metal. For QT2 this is the only finish coat. For QT3 this is the first of two coats. No LRV restriction — any color permitted.

tasks.name: Finish Coat 1 — Spray Application
tasks.description: Spray-apply first finish coat of 100% acrylic exterior latex. Even coverage, consistent mil build. No backbrushing — aluminum is non-porous metal. Standard spray tips (413-515). Any color permitted — no LRV restriction on aluminum.

quality_notes.QT2: Even coverage. No drips or holidays. Single pass sufficient.
quality_notes.QT3: Uniform mil build. No visible spray pattern at 6 ft. Consistent appearance across all elevations.

tasks.name: Finish Coat 1 — Brush/Roll Application
tasks.description: Brush and roll first finish coat when spray is not feasible. Roller with 3/8 inch nap for open field, brush at edges and transitions.

quality_notes.QT3: Even coverage. No brush marks in roller field. Maintain wet edge.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: First finish coat after primer system has cured (self-etching primer, or epoxy intermediate for coastal). Method determined by application_method. QT2 = final coat. QT3 proceeds to coat 2.

sop_modules.name: Finish Coat 2
sop_modules.description: Second (final) finish coat. QT3 only — QT2 uses single finish coat. No interstage sanding between coats (aluminum surface does not require intercoat abrasion on non-porous metal).

tasks.name: Finish Coat 2 — Spray Application
tasks.description: Second and final finish coat by spray. Critical for full hide, proper DFT, and maximum durability. Allow recoat time per TDS between coats. No backbrushing.

quality_notes.QT3: Uniform mil build. Consistent appearance across all elevations. No visible spray pattern at 6 ft.

tasks.name: Finish Coat 2 — Brush/Roll Application
tasks.description: Second and final finish coat by brush and roller.

quality_notes.QT3: Even coverage. No brush marks in roller field. Maintain wet edge to natural break points.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Second and final finish coat. QT3 only. Allow recoat time per TDS. QT2 stops after coat 1. No interstage sanding needed on aluminum.

sop_modules.name: Brush Detail — J-Channels & Transitions
sop_modules.description: Brush detail at J-channels, under-sill channels, corner transitions, and trim cut-in. QT3 only — primary labor differentiator between tiers. Same function as vinyl detail module.

tasks.name: Brush Detail — J-Channels & Under-Sill
tasks.description: Brush-apply finish coat into J-channels, under-sill channels, and starter strip recesses. Spray may not fully penetrate these recessed areas — brush ensures full coating coverage in channels.

quality_notes.QT3: Full coverage in all channel recesses. No bare aluminum visible in channels. Clean transitions at channel-to-field junction.

tasks.name: Brush Cut-In at Trim Transitions
tasks.description: Brush cut-in where siding meets corner trim, window casing, door casing, and soffit junction. Clean color line at siding-to-trim boundary.

quality_notes.QT3: Sharp color line at trim boundary. No bleed onto trim surface. Consistent line at 6 ft viewing.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Detail work after final spray coat has set (tack-free). J-channels first, then trim cut-in. QT3 only.

sop_modules.name: Cleanup & Demobilization
sop_modules.description: Final walkthrough inspection, touch-up, remove all protection materials, clean spray equipment, scaffold teardown, site restoration. No RRP cleanup required (aluminum factory-baked enamel is not lead-based).

tasks.name: Final Walkthrough Inspection
tasks.description: Walk all elevations and inspect completed siding finish for defects, holidays, coverage, and appearance. Check DFT readings from primer phase documentation.

quality_notes.QT2: Ground-level walkthrough at 10 ft viewing distance.
quality_notes.QT3: Ground-level walkthrough at 6 ft viewing distance. Binoculars for upper elevations. Review DFT log from primer phase.

tasks.name: Final Touch-Up
tasks.description: Brush touch-up of defects found during final walkthrough inspection.

quality_notes.QT2: Fix obvious defects at ground-level viewing distance.
quality_notes.QT3: Fix all noted defects. Blend seamlessly at 6 ft.

tasks.name: Remove All Protection Materials
tasks.description: Remove all masking tape, masking paper/film, drop cloths, plastic sheeting, landscape tarps, fixture bags, and HVAC covers.

quality_notes.all: All tape, plastic, paper, and tarps removed. Check for adhesive residue on fixtures and trim. Clean any overspray on windows or doors.

tasks.name: Scaffold / Lift Teardown
tasks.description: Dismantle scaffold, return aerial lift, or stage ladders for removal.

quality_notes.all: All access equipment removed. No damage to landscaping or hardscape from equipment.

tasks.name: Clean Spray Equipment & Tools
tasks.description: Flush airless sprayer, clean spray tips and filters. CRITICAL: flush thoroughly between self-etching primer and finish coat — primer chemistry is incompatible with acrylic finish if cross-contaminated. Clean brushes and rollers.

quality_notes.all: Equipment fully flushed and clean. Self-etching primer residue MUST be fully purged before finish coat — cross-contamination causes adhesion failure. Spray tips inspected. Filters replaced if needed.

tasks.name: Final Site Cleanup & Demobilization
tasks.description: Collect all debris — empty containers, tape, masking paper, sheeting, rags, used abrasive pads. Restore site to pre-work condition. Load equipment and demobilize. Rinse hardscape if alkaline cleaner residue remains from wash phase.

quality_notes.all: Site restored to pre-work condition. All debris removed. No paint splatter on hardscape or landscape. Neutralize alkaline cleaner residue on hardscape with water rinse.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Final inspect → Touch-up → Remove protection → Scaffold teardown → Clean equipment → Site cleanup & demobilization.

round_configurations.description: Economy aluminum repaint: wash → protect → chalk verify → oxide scuff → self-etching prime (1 coat, 0.5-1.0 mil) → 1 finish coat → cleanup
round_configurations.notes: Minimum viable aluminum repaint. Self-etching primer mandatory. Single finish coat. No detail module. No caulk. Total: 2 coating passes (self-etch prime + 1 finish).

round_configurations.description: Standard aluminum repaint: wash → protect → chalk verify → oxide scuff → caulk → self-etching prime (1 coat, 0.5-1.0 mil) → 2 finish coats → detail → cleanup
round_configurations.notes: Standard residential aluminum repaint. Two finish coats for full hide and durability. J-channel detail. Caulk assessment. Total: 3 coating passes (self-etch prime + 2 finish) + detail.

round_configurations.description: Coastal economy aluminum repaint: wash → protect → chalk verify → oxide scuff → self-etching prime → epoxy intermediate → 1 finish coat → cleanup
round_configurations.notes: Coastal variant adds epoxy intermediate between self-etching primer and finish. Three-layer corrosion barrier system. Total: 3 coating passes (self-etch + epoxy + 1 finish).

round_configurations.description: Coastal standard aluminum repaint: wash → protect → chalk verify → oxide scuff → caulk → self-etching prime → epoxy intermediate → 2 finish coats → detail → cleanup
round_configurations.notes: Coastal variant with full coat system. Three-layer corrosion barrier + two finish coats + detail. Total: 4 coating passes (self-etch + epoxy + 2 finish) + detail.

protection_zones.description: Adjacent landscape beds, shrubs, and plantings — extended coverage for chalk-laden wash runoff
protection_zones.spray_escalation: Extend coverage from 3 ft to 10 ft for spray overspray zone

protection_zones.description: Window glass and frame masking for spray operations
Exterior door masking for spray operations
Trim masking at siding-to-trim transitions for spray
Soffit/fascia at eave junction — overspray protection
protection_zones.notes: Roofline masking handled as part of trim mask setup when soffit is different color from siding.

aluminum_specific_tasks: TSK_ALRP_CHALK_VERIFY — mandatory chalk verification gate (all substrate states)
TSK_ALRP_OXIDE_SCUFF — Al2O3 oxide layer scuff with synthetic abrasive pads
TSK_ALRP_DFT_VERIFY — DFT gauge verification on self-etching primer (0.5-1.0 mil)
TSK_ALRP_PRIME_ETCH_SPRAY — self-etching primer spray (phosphoric acid + zinc)
TSK_ALRP_WASH_CHALK_HEAVY — heavy chalk multi-pass wash protocol

exclusions.reason: Aluminum siding manufacturer warranties have typically expired. Factory-baked enamel warranty does not void upon repainting. Unlike vinyl where warranty void acknowledgment is mandatory.

Aluminum has no LRV restriction — any color permitted. Aluminum conducts heat efficiently, no thermal warping risk. Melting point (1220 F) vastly exceeds solar gain temperatures. No IR-reflective product requirement.
Aluminum siding factory-baked enamel is not lead-based. Even earliest residential aluminum siding (1940s) used baked enamel, not lead paint. EPA RRP does not apply.
Aluminum has two substrate states (SS_EXT_SOUND_PAINT, SS_EXT_CHALKING) but no DSD gradient. Condition is assessed via chalk_severity dimension, not DSD survey.
Factory-baked enamel on aluminum does not peel in sheets like paint on wood. Chalking is the primary degradation mode, not flaking. No loose material to scrape.

exclusions.excluded_item: Backbrushing tasks on any spray application
exclusions.reason: Aluminum is non-porous metal. Coating does not absorb into substrate. Backbrushing serves no purpose on aluminum.
Primed aluminum surface provides adequate adhesion for topcoat without intercoat sanding. Non-porous metal does not require intercoat abrasion.
Aluminum siding is not a fine-finish substrate. QT4/QT5 excluded per resolution.
Aluminum does not absorb water. Moisture content testing is a wood-specific concern.
Aluminum factory finish is always baked enamel — not an unknown coating. No coating type ambiguity.

No LRV restriction on aluminum. Single finish system (SYS_EXT_ALRP_FINISH_ACRYLIC) for all colors. No IR-reflective product path needed. Simpler than vinyl (which splits standard vs IR-reflective by LRV class).

assumptions.value: Chalk verification gate is mandatory for ALL substrate states including SS_EXT_SOUND_PAINT
assumptions.note: Even sound-paint state may have hidden chalk in sheltered areas. Residual chalk is a bond-breaker for self-etching primer.

assumptions.value: Oxide scuff and self-etching primer MUST be scheduled same-day — aluminum re-oxidizes within 4-8 hours (2-4 hours coastal)
assumptions.note: If delay unavoidable, re-scuff before priming. SOP enforces same-day sequencing.

assumptions.value: DFT verification task included in both QT2 and QT3 — over-application risk exists at all quality tiers
assumptions.note: DFT verification is not a quality add-on — it is a quality assurance gate to prevent cohesive failure. Included at both tiers. More verification locations at QT3.

assumptions.value: Self-etching primer application requires lead-level skill — DFT control is critical and failure mode is counter-intuitive (more primer = worse)
assumptions.note: Standard primers do not have this constraint. Self-etching primer DFT control in field conditions (height, wind, angle) requires experienced applicator.

assumptions.value: No interstage sanding or inspection module between finish coats
assumptions.note: Non-porous metal surface does not require intercoat sanding.

assumptions.value: Brush detail at J-channels and cut-in is QT3 only — primary labor differentiator between tiers
Three separate wash tasks by chalk_severity rather than a single scaled task
assumptions.note: Heavy chalk wash is fundamentally different work (multi-pass, mechanical scrubbing) not just slower. Separate tasks model the distinct work scope. FAC_ALRP_CHALK modifier scales production rates.
